commit.message:
Preserve local launch permissions across TUI sessions and reconnects (#49809)

## Why

Explicit launch permissions such as `--yolo` can be lost during reconnect recovery, causing subsequent input to use different approval and sandbox settings.

## What changed

Remember explicit local launch approval policies, approvals reviewers, and permission profiles at startup and when creating new sessions. Restore the approvals reviewer independently of profile overrides during reconnect recovery. Keep constrained profiles that cannot be expressed through legacy turn parameters under server control.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for `--yolo` across new sessions and reconnects, later permission-picker choices, reviewer-only overrides, and server-owned constrained profiles. Extend the reconnect integration test to submit the preserved draft and verify its approval and sandbox settings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7a77dc41b2a357ab17fec9ba6cb2361f4a8f4aa5

Enable API-key model discovery by default (#49807)

## What changed

- Mark `api_key_model_discovery` as stable and enable it by default, while preserving explicit user opt-outs and provider catalog requirements.
- Fall back to bundled models when discovery is disabled at runtime, including when a remote catalog has already been loaded.

## Testing

Extend model-list coverage for default enablement, app overrides, and user configuration precedence. Add a regression assertion that runtime opt-outs hide loaded catalogs without additional fetches, and update daemon compatibility tests for the new default.

GitOrigin-RevId: feaf732757792cc58063f21a5327d0e633f079f4

Accept unknown Codex error variants in the app-server protocol (#49806)

## Why

New error variants should not prevent older clients from handling app-server errors.

## What changed

- Deserialize unknown `CodexErrorInfo` strings and objects as `Other` in Rust, while preserving known variants and the `"other"` serialization.
- Allow arbitrary strings and objects in the exported JSON schemas and TypeScript type.
- Update Python SDK generation and generated models to accept unknown error strings and object payloads.

## Testing

Add Rust tests for `"other"` round trips, unknown string and object fallbacks, known structured variants, and rejection of null, boolean, numeric, and array values.

GitOrigin-RevId: 40c17896019924b2ef7970ee2205ea0154d0d1b3

Add capability-gated writable file streams to the exec-server client (#49805)

## Why

Older executors can ignore the file open mode and silently return a read-only handle for a writable open.

## What changed

Add `ExecServerClient::fs_write_block` and require the `file_write_streaming` capability for both block writes and `FsOpenMode::Replace` opens. Return a protocol error before sending either request when the executor lacks support, while allowing read-only opens.

## Testing

Add a WebSocket regression test verifying that unsupported writable opens and block writes are rejected locally and read-only opens still reach the executor.

GitOrigin-RevId: f206e1da80c12af76ead14c75f8ffe71f82cce89

Use platform-specific modifier labels in TUI shortcut hints (#49804)

## What changed

Render Control, Shift, and Alt as `⌃`, `⇧`, and `⌥` on macOS, and Control as `^` on Linux. Keep textual modifier labels on other platforms.

Route hard-coded shortcut hints through the shared key-label formatter so footers, overlays, pickers, and transcript notices use consistent notation.

## Testing

Update modifier-combination and chord label assertions, along with rendering snapshots and narrow-layout expectations for the shorter hints.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0d20fa218e4a11dfe7a81c8de64f8d25e093af03

Update the Rust toolchain action for argument-comment linting (#49801)

## What changed

Pin `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` to a revision from `master` in the argument-comment lint package CI and release build workflows. Both continue to request `nightly-2026-08-20`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 63801f669b91d4bfa1d69fc05d728d838ca8add0

Allow cleanup of replay-only side conversations with missing threads (#49800)

## Why

A saved side conversation transcript can outlive its ephemeral server thread. The resulting `turn/interrupt` error prevented side conversation cleanup and blocked archiving the parent thread.

## What changed

Treat the specific `thread not found` interrupt error as successful interruption for replay-only side conversations, allowing unsubscribe and local cleanup to finish. Continue sending interrupt requests because replay-only conversations may still be running after reconnect.

## Testing

Expand archive lifecycle coverage for local daemon and remote server connections to include live side conversations, replay-only conversations with existing threads, and replay-only conversations whose threads are gone. Assert that interruption, unsubscribe, archiving, and local cleanup occur.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0528c9f5b5278931fd3a7941073071117f2f3612

Preserve server web-search settings in the TUI (#49799)

## Why

The TUI unconditionally forwarded its resolved `web_search` mode, allowing implicit client settings to replace server defaults or saved thread settings.

## What changed

- Forward `web_search` on thread start, resume, and fork only when the winning choice comes from session flags or a selected profile.
- Translate legacy search feature flags into a canonical `web_search` override while preserving precedence, and remove those flags from forwarded feature overrides.
- Honor shared feature requirements for embedded sessions while letting remote servers enforce their own requirements on explicit search choices.

## Testing

Add coverage for configuration origins, canonical and legacy search precedence, and embedded versus remote feature requirements. Extend the Responses integration test to verify that a remote server's live search setting survives thread start and resume when the client's configuration disables search.

GitOrigin-RevId: c714f9cf0321aca9a5fa292a350720af5a2d02d4

Share cached exec-server environment info with Arc (#49798)

## What changed

Return `Arc<EnvironmentInfo>` from `ExecServerClient::environment_info()` so repeated reads and cloned clients share cached metadata without cloning its contents. Wrap metadata from initialization and lazy RPC fetches in `Arc`, while preserving the owned return value in `LazyRemoteExecServerClient`.

## Testing

Extend the cache test to assert pointer identity across cloned clients for both initialization-provided metadata and lazy fetching after connecting to a legacy server.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3f56f4d51a4aebc0c4821c0b128a70efb23933d4

Deduplicate Guardian retained-context omission notices (#49796)

## Why

Guardian review continuations can repeat retained-instruction omission notices even when availability has not changed. When retained context becomes complete, earlier notices also need to be superseded explicitly.

## What changed

Track delivered user-instruction and assistant-context omission states in host metadata scoped to the retained-instructions section. Suppress redundant notice-only sections when the state is unchanged, and emit an availability-change notice when an earlier omission clears, including when no retained originals remain.

Treat missing delivery metadata as unknown. Matching notice text in coalesced tool output cannot establish host delivery, and incomplete history entries discard omission delivery proof.

## Testing

Add coverage for repeated notices, independent histories, availability recovery, and matching notice text in multimodal REPL output. Extend app-server review-continuation tests to assert that each effective classifier context contains the retained user-instruction omission notice exactly once.

GitOrigin-RevId: c6d52dd1dafb284af34b46174aecc7c8cc9b8404

Avoid duplicate sync reviews in Guardian classifier continuations (#49795)

## Why

Retained Guardian classifier conversations already contain previously delivered synchronous reviews. Appending those reviews again repeats evidence and consumes input budget.

## What changed

Track each review completion with a stable identity in host-only history metadata. Filter already delivered reviews before composing and budgeting continuation input, while preserving distinct completions even when their text is identical.

Fresh conversations receive the review evidence again, and shortened messages no longer count as complete delivery. Delivery metadata stays out of model requests.

## Testing

Add coverage for delivering retained reviews once, appending newly completed reviews, restoring evidence after failed streams, and retaining reviews when history lacks complete delivery metadata.

GitOrigin-RevId: b8d58ffdd7d9c484676af707c65fa50020aae73c

Add conversation mode to Guardian v2 async classification (#49793)

## What changed

- Add `features.guardianv2.async_classifier_mode` with `snapshot` and `conversation` modes. Local configuration overrides model defaults; snapshots remain the fallback.
- Retain completed classifier requests and responses in conversation mode, appending transcript deltas without repeating previously delivered user instructions.
- Rebuild retained history when authorization, classifier instructions, or parent compaction changes, after an incomplete response, or when the next request exceeds the configured token limit. Add `async_classifier_conversation_token_limit`, defaulting to 100,000 tokens, while preserving the model's input limit for fresh requests.
- Serialize conversation requests in observation order, bound outstanding work, and reject stale work after authorization changes or thread shutdown. Record retained and new input token costs.

## Testing

Add tests for configuration precedence, history reuse and resets, ordered admission, queue overflow, and stale or stopped requests. Exercise the approval matrix in both modes, including resume, fork, mandatory review, authorization changes, and stream failure after an early score.

GitOrigin-RevId: 35b9800104648cde4f467086e678dee12458c3e5

Add retained conversation support to Guardian async sampling (#49792)

## What changed

- Add request preparation that preserves committed classifier history and appends transcript deltas, filtering instructions and images already delivered. Account for the complete input budget before transferring history; rejected requests leave the checkpoint and cursor intact.
- Add retained sampling that publishes the early score while collecting completed assistant output and encrypted reasoning for reuse. Preserve item IDs and input metadata, and discard unusable history without retracting an already published score.
- Keep the existing snapshot sampling path and share input preparation and execution with the new retained path. Retained sampling is not yet wired into the active backend.

## Testing

Add coverage for transcript and image deduplication, immutable history prefixes, budget boundaries, rejected preparation, WebSocket output retention, and retention failures that preserve the early score.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0fa33db8b8ea4483eb64d75e207690f1d349123b

Remove `AGENTS.md` from Bazel core test data (#49787)

## What changed

Remove the repository-root `AGENTS.md` from `codex-rs/core` test data and from the root Bazel `exports_files` list.

GitOrigin-RevId: 644052d50f79b4c798baf40e53aab824f0fd73c3

Clarify V2 spawn model override guidance for context catalogs (#49786)

## What changed

When the model catalog is provided in context and model overrides are exposed, tell V2 `spawn_agent` callers to inherit the current model unless the user explicitly asks for a different model. Include this guidance even when spawn metadata is hidden.

## Testing

Extend tool-description tests to cover hidden metadata with both inline and context catalogs, and update request-level assertions for V1 and V2 model override guidance.

GitOrigin-RevId: b70b0f09b0b5987a0eccba578196b8ef7cee4baf

Persist empty paginated threads when naming them (#49785)

## Why

Naming a paginated thread before its first turn must make it durable so it can be resumed immediately and after an app-server restart.

## What changed

Persist the live rollout before updating name metadata in SQLite. Propagate persistence failures before saving the name.

## Testing

Add thread-store tests for empty-thread persistence and failure handling, plus an app-server regression test that resumes a named empty thread before and after a restart and completes its first turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2f7556c7de65f6a86177130c39e1a17951496931

Add a requirements feature gate for the browser annotation API (#49784)

## What changed

Register `browser_annotation_api` as a stable, default-enabled feature intended for requirements rather than user configuration. It controls websites opening and customizing annotation tools in desktop apps, independently of ordinary user-driven annotation.

Add the key to the configuration schema, extending the browser requirements support introduced in https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/18956.

## Testing

Extend `browser_feature_requirements_are_valid` to verify that enterprise requirements setting `browser_annotation_api = false` disable the feature.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8c7bb65932e08560040958b4472fe45f6d1c916f

Preserve background thread requests when forking in the TUI (#49783)

## Why

Switching to a fork can interrupt approval routing for source and child threads that remain on a local daemon or remote app server. Their pending requests and event listeners need to survive the switch.

## What changed

- Retain background request routing and event listeners for tracked threads when switching to a daemon-backed fork, preserving pending approvals without duplicating them.
- Register the source thread before the `fork_thread` tool creates a fork so its requests remain routable during the operation.
- Route requests for the currently viewed thread to the active UI, even when that thread is also tracked in the agents overview.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for local daemon and remote forks retaining source and child threads, replaying pending requests when returning to the source, and displaying active-thread file-change approvals. Verify that embedded forks still discard the source thread state and that `fork_thread` registers its source before issuing the fork request.

GitOrigin-RevId: 63139e2b9a6eff373ab05a31e0140a432ce47389

Clean up process groups for failed shell snapshot captures (#49782)

## Why

Failed shell snapshot captures could leave processes launched by shell startup files running after the capture ended.

## What changed

Run each Unix shell snapshot capture in its own process group and kill that group on failure, timeout, or cancellation. Keep the capture leader unreaped until output and exit status are validated so its process group ID cannot be reused during cleanup. Preserve startup helpers after a successful capture.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for startup child cleanup after nonzero exits, invalid output, cancellation, and timeout, alongside fallback and retry behavior. Verify that successful captures preserve delayed startup output and background services and reuse the cached snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: a56ef5d8615325952bdc8bb78727de1559e7e9c7

Include the environment's MXC backend in MCP sandbox metadata (#49781)

## What changed

Capture each environment's effective Windows sandbox backend in the MCP runtime and include it as `useMxc` in sandbox state metadata for supporting servers. Use the server's captured environment selection, including local fallback, so the local MXC preference does not leak into attached environments. Default missing backend information to `false`.

## Testing

Extend tests to cover MXC metadata handoff, attachment isolation, local fallback without a selected local environment, and preservation of captured backend settings across runtime refreshes.

GitOrigin-RevId: f559bffeff383838334e5a475b1eab608d571fa1

Define exec-server protocol types for streamed file writes (#49778)

## What changed

- Add `read` and `replace` modes to `fs/open`, defaulting omitted modes to `read` for existing callers.
- Define `fs/writeBlock` request and response types for offset-based writes, with a maximum decoded chunk size of 1 MiB.
- Add the `fileWriteStreaming` capability, defaulting to `false`. Keep writable streams unsupported in the server and explicitly reject replacement opens.

## Testing

Add a protocol test verifying that legacy `fs/open` requests without a mode deserialize as read-only opens.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4d3997717e821cd1f62df12a03c8eec36332a66d

Add account security setup reminders to the TUI (#49715)

## What changed

Fetch optional security setup notices asynchronously for local ChatGPT sessions using the OpenAI provider. Verify that saved credentials match the connected app server, ignore stale account responses, and validate notice text and HTTPS actions on `chatgpt.com`.

Show notices as dismissible inline banners with a browser action, while giving applicable usage banners priority. Preserve notice state and dismissal across thread changes, reconnects, and banner replacement for the same account and user.

## Testing

Add authenticated HTTP fixture tests, notice validation tests, and TUI tests covering stale responses, dismissal persistence, usage banner priority, browser actions, and wrapping in narrow terminals.

GitOrigin-RevId: b8635fcf6a26b42b6a06640601c8517d8d5e47e8

Decouple API-key cyber access programs from model discovery (#49714)

## What changed

Allow API-key sessions using the OpenAI provider to forward explicit cyber access programs when `features.api_key_cyber_access_programs` is enabled, regardless of `features.api_key_model_discovery`.

## Testing

Expand the app-server test to cover all four combinations of the two feature flags, checking forwarded programs and failures when forwarding is disabled. Default the API-key test helper to model discovery disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: f9cf1d2bd7c231645d50178cc6721b55a8d63268

Remove repository-local Codex guidance, skills, and environment config (#49713)

## What changed

Delete the root `AGENTS.md`, the skills under `.codex/skills/` and their supporting scripts, tests, and references, and `.codex/environments/environment.toml`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 555482804c79d17f9aa5587c4d26ea03337db8d9

Avoid full-string scans in token-budget truncation (#49712)

## Why

Token-budget truncation uses byte counts to estimate tokens, but previously scanned the entire string to count characters, including the discarded middle.

## What changed

Use UTF-8 boundary lookups to select the retained prefix and suffix for token-budget truncation. Skip character counting for a zero-token budget and defer it to paths that need character counts.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for multibyte characters crossing both retained boundaries, checking the truncated output and original token estimate.

GitOrigin-RevId: 37fee0c8d4ede8e74b491d3d641b0ea0e9003dd4

Classify SQLite corruption using typed error codes (#49710)

## What changed

Preserve the underlying error in `LocalStateDbStartupError` and use its error chain to decide whether CLI startup failures qualify for automatic database backup and recovery.

Replace corruption checks against error-message text with SQLite result-code classification, including SQLx extended result codes and directly wrapped `SqliteError` values.

## Testing

Update the embedded startup corruption test to verify that the startup error retains a detectable SQLite corruption cause and the failed database path.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6e8ecd0ee67f3c239183ddea3fc75c4e4cd5744a

Move session index I/O off async runtime threads (#49708)

## Why

Session index updates perform synchronous file I/O and wait on a blocking mutex inside async functions, blocking runtime threads.

## What changed

Run appends and thread-name removals in `spawn_blocking` workers. Acquire a Tokio mutex before dispatch and keep its owned guard in the worker so queued and running updates remain serialized even if the awaiting task is cancelled. Move the lookup's file-existence check into its blocking worker as well.

## Testing

Add tests for lock retention after cancellation of running and queued updates, write ordering after cancellation, and removal that preserves other thread names and malformed lines.

GitOrigin-RevId: 368745d8e5bbf24c527facc0a62ddd0fb76f0ffb

Upgrade the argument comment lint toolchain and Dylint (#49706)

## What changed

- Move the lint to `nightly-2026-08-20` and Dylint `6.1.0`, updating CI, release artifacts, Bazel configuration, and installation instructions.
- Adapt to the updated rustc and Clippy APIs, including resolving `Option::None` through type aliases when checking for uncommented arguments.
- Set the `chatgpt` crate's `recursion_limit` to `256`.

## Testing

Extend the UI fixture to expect an uncommented-argument warning for `OptionalString::None`, where `OptionalString` aliases `Option<String>`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 34e1b173972f0bfa9b6c8fd3342ca652539efe2f

Prevent npm alpha dist-tags from moving backward (#49704)

## Why

Publishing an older alpha or alpha hotfix can overwrite npm dist-tags that already point to a newer release.

## What changed

Check each package's current npm dist-tag before publishing an alpha release, using the existing release version comparison and workflow concurrency lock. Handle `alpha` and platform-specific tags independently for Codex, the SDK, and the responses API proxy.

When the release does not advance the current version, publish under `release-<version>-<tag>` to keep it installable without changing the alpha or `latest` tags. Abort publishing if the registry lookup fails.

## Testing

Add unit tests for package and platform tag selection, older releases, dotted alpha hotfixes, missing tags, and registry lookup failures.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9c0edec1149bf78c01aac0f700e963630316eaea

Rename exec-server file handle management identifiers (#49702)

## What changed

Rename `file_read` to `file_handle` and `FileReadHandleManager` to `FileHandleManager`. Update the filesystem handler field, handle ID validation helper, and related constants to use file handle terminology. File operations, limits, and error messages remain unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: 25ad81a917386da23fd42ecff79bd47a482ce430

Detect SQLite corruption during startup and preserve recovery backups (#49701)

## Why

A database can open successfully while containing corruption that startup previously missed. Detecting it before runtime initialization completes allows recoverable databases to be rebuilt while preserving the damaged files.

## What changed

- Run `PRAGMA quick_check(1)` when opening writable databases, with a 100 ms scan budget. Share attempts across cloned `SqliteConfig` instances by file identity so repeated opens skip validation and replacement files are checked again.
- Back up and rebuild runtime databases that support recovery. Report corruption without rebuilding thread history or other databases without an automatic recovery policy. Treat interrupted or locked checks as incomplete rather than confirmed corruption.
- Collect startup backups across recovery retries and include their locations in the app server warning. Explain that saved conversations can restore the thread list and history, while some database-only metadata may be unavailable.
- Record confirmed corruption in `codex.sqlite.corruption.count`.

## Testing

Add tests for recovery policies, backup preservation, validation caching and concurrency, cancelled and interrupted checks, and locked databases. Add app server coverage for recovery warnings and saved conversation restoration, a TUI warning snapshot, and message board post preservation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 43e26328888e0301def642d69bd324acee867566

Make exec-server file reads cancellable between chunks (#49696)

## What changed

Run direct `read_file` operations in a blocking task with bounded read chunks and cancellation checks. Dropping the async caller cancels further reads between chunks. Preserve the 512 MiB size limit, symlink-following options, and regular-file validation.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for 4 MiB reads and oversized-file rejection with both symlink-following options, cancellation after the first chunk, and FIFO rejection without waiting for a writer.

GitOrigin-RevId: 19f2816de15a03bd89b463de6b002367e6a692a9

Batch rollout listing scans on cancellable blocking workers (#49694)

## What changed

Move directory enumeration and candidate metadata lookups into blocking workers, batching updated-time candidate collection into one worker per scan. Check cancellation between entries and metadata lookups so dropping the async waiter stops further scanning.

Share synchronous rollout metadata resolution with the async helper, preserving plain-file precedence over compressed siblings. Retain scan limits, stable file ordering, and directory-level early stopping for creation-time listings.

## Testing

Add tests for cancellation during directory enumeration and candidate discovery in both flat and date-partitioned layouts, including plain-sibling metadata precedence and filtering of unrelated files, directories, and symlinks.

GitOrigin-RevId: 324289003b29a7d2b3220da03e3c002ab5e23eec

Move thread history projection into one blocking task (#49693)

## What changed

Run rollout file opening, metadata lookup, seeking, reading, and record
projection together in a single `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` call. Use
synchronous file I/O in `read_projection_steps_sync` and carry the current
tracing span into the blocking task.

GitOrigin-RevId: a231a8b9a328f6d2e2095a29cde1718ccb6b3901

Keep compressed rollout snippet searches on one blocking worker (#49692)

## Why

Compressed snippet searches schedule a blocking task for every line read. Keeping the scan on one worker avoids repeated task scheduling.

## What changed

Use `RolloutLineReader::find_map` to scan compressed rollouts on a single blocking worker, stopping at the first matching snippet. Preserve read metrics and stop delivering records when the search is canceled, including cancellation during a read.

## Testing

Add tests for first-match snippets, case-insensitive literal matching, malformed records, missing matches, stream errors before a match, and cancellation between lines or during a read.

GitOrigin-RevId: 295206b1a00e861bc44606bd843f6ed8c3e6aae1

Preserve PowerShell relative paths in the elevated Windows sandbox (#49690)

## Why

An inaccessible user profile directory can prevent sandboxed PowerShell from preserving its working directory and resolving relative paths in a project beneath that profile.

## What changed

Pass `USERPROFILE` to elevated setup and refresh. When the command's working directory is beneath an absolute profile path, grant the sandbox group non-inheriting `FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES` access to the profile directory.

Preserve existing permissions and deny ACEs during non-inheriting ACL updates without propagating changes to descendants. Expand generic deny masks when checking for conflicting permissions.

## Testing

Add a Windows regression test that checks PowerShell's working directory and reading `.\public.txt` beneath a protected profile. Add an ACL test that verifies a non-inheriting grant leaves an unprotected child's security descriptor unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7f142a7ffdee795c3255d4a6e79568fa9391c055

Export skill invocation events through OpenTelemetry (#49689)

## What changed

Emit `codex.skill_invocation` logs for explicit skill injection and detected implicit use, including skill-tool reads. Include skill name, invocation type, conversation, turn, model, and client metadata, plus scope, plugin ID, and ChatGPT user and account IDs when available.

Exclude skill contents, resource paths, email addresses, prompts, and tool payloads. Use the existing OTEL log exporter without an additional opt-in; `otel.exporter = "none"` continues to export no logs.

Document the event fields, exporter configuration, and detection semantics in `codex-rs/otel/README.md`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0f9c492c3f224455f3de3660be89692d776c1951

Deliver remote message board notifications to active turns (#49686)

## What changed

- Start a turn-owned notification receiver using the same remote board client and session identity as the board tools. Deliver post previews as agent messages and cancel the receiver when the turn stops, aborts, or errors.
- Wait for the initial connection attempt before inference, then retry failed or disconnected streams without waking idle agents.
- Skip malformed notices, mismatched recipients or turns, and oversized previews. Reject delivery to stale or canceled turns and bound remote notices to a 1 KiB context budget.

## Testing

Extend remote board tests to cover interrupted setup, connection failures, reconnection, invalid and stale notices, preview delivery into model context, and receiver shutdown after turn completion.

GitOrigin-RevId: c7c8d977fe74b7a5cb3bd8216dc0146f3f297e44

Add a managed feature gate for in-app voice (#49683)

## What changed

Register `in_app_voice` as a stable, default-enabled feature and add it to the configuration schema. The gate is intended for managed requirements to control permission for voice in desktop apps; permission does not establish voice availability or provider support.

## Testing

Add app-server coverage for reporting `in_app_voice = false` from `requirements.toml` in both requirements and feature-list responses. Extend the CLI feature-list test to verify that cloud-managed requirements disable the gate despite a user-configured `true` value, without rewriting the user configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ec3bc0176fdb3e1714b0136bf812bd56591f6a1

Escape command drafts when recovering question answers (#49678)

## Why

When a turn ends, recovered question answers are appended to the composer draft. If that draft starts with a shell or slash command, submitting the combined text can interpret it as a command instead of a prompt.

## What changed

Escape command prefixes before appending recovered answers so the combined draft stays editable and submits as literal prompt text. Convert shell mode's separate `!` prefix into escaped composer text, and leave slash-prefixed paths such as `/tmp/file` unchanged.

Keep prefix escaping and answer recovery in the same Vim undo edit.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for immediate and queued submission, whitespace around command prefixes, slash-prefixed paths, and already escaped commands. Extend Vim undo coverage to shell and slash command drafts, including shell mode, and add a snapshot of the recovered shell draft.

GitOrigin-RevId: 03c40f72a834a65bf367103cb9170a86dc35ad98

Serialize Responses routing fields before large inputs (#49675)

## Why

Gateways that inspect request bodies incrementally need routing fields before potentially multi-megabyte prompts so they can route requests without buffering the input first.

## What changed

Serialize `model`, `stream`, and optional `service_tier` before `input` in both HTTP Responses requests and WebSocket `response.create` messages. Preserve field values and omission of unset `service_tier`.

## Testing

Add an HTTP regression test with a 2 MiB input that checks routing field order and unchanged JSON contents. Extend WebSocket serialization coverage to assert the routing fields appear first, and check that HTTP requests omit unset `service_tier`.

GitOrigin-RevId: dbc174e1fe7ca30d0c00f075bc37dd5f97b27b37

Allow managed requirements to disable the Windows MXC sandbox (#49642)

## Why

`windows.allowed_sandbox_implementations` permits MXC regardless of the listed implementations. Managed requirements need a separate way to block both explicit MXC configuration and automatic selection through `prefer_mxc`.

## What changed

Add the optional managed requirement `windows.allow_mxc`. Setting it to `false` disables automatic MXC selection and rejects explicit `windows.sandbox = "mxc"` configuration with an error identifying the requirement. Leaving it unset or setting it to `true` preserves existing behavior.

## Testing

Add coverage for the requirement alongside allowed sandbox implementations, preference resolution, and cloud-managed opt-out behavior for implicit, elevated, and explicit MXC configurations.

GitOrigin-RevId: a458a7b4c92cf17e687dbbad8208884d1c097da5

Use server authentication for explicit remote session commands (#49624)

## Why

Session commands with `--remote` should use the selected server's authentication and execution environment, even when the caller has workload identity configured and cannot read its identity token.

## What changed

Connect `queue`, `archive`, `unarchive`, and `delete` directly to the explicit remote app server after validating configuration. Skip caller credential and runtime initialization, use remote thread parameters, and preserve the caller's working-directory override.

## Testing

Add end-to-end coverage with an unreadable caller identity token to verify queued turns use the server's API key and remote archive, unarchive, and deletion operate on the selected server. Add configuration-validation coverage for all four commands and `--no-daemon` rejection coverage for remote unarchive and delete.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5da7abbb40506cd754a8863e1a9d8fad9b1f09a9

Reuse unchanged history snapshots when resuming threads (#49600)

## Why

Resuming a thread rereads persisted history even when a preloaded snapshot is unchanged. Reusing that snapshot must still account for writes committed before writer ownership is acquired.

## What changed

- Carry optional, non-serialized revisions from stored history and model context through thread and agent resume paths.
- Validate the revision under writer ownership and reuse the shared snapshot when it matches. Reload stored history when the revision is missing or changed, while preserving explicit history overrides.
- Resolve the selected rollout before loading context, validate compressed snapshots before materialization, and enforce archived-thread restrictions on canonical paths.

## Testing

Clean up canceled exec-server RPC requests immediately (#49332)

## Why

Canceled RPC calls could leave entries in the pending request map until further traffic or disconnect. Cleanup should happen when the call is dropped, even if no response arrives.

## What changed

Use a `PendingRequestGuard` to remove each registration when its call completes or is canceled. Protect the pending map with a synchronous mutex so cleanup can run in `Drop`, replacing opportunistic pruning and explicit error-path removals.

## Testing

Add a regression test that drops an in-flight call and verifies that the pending request count immediately reaches zero without further traffic.

Keep remote control reconnect backoff capped during sustained failures (#49330)

## Why

Reaching the reconnect backoff cap reset the attempt counter, restarting fast retries during sustained failures such as HTTP 409 responses indicating that the remote app server is already online.

## What changed

Keep the reconnect delay at the 30-second cap and stop advancing the backoff exponent once capped. Successful connections and auth changes still reset backoff. Remove logging for the obsolete reset-at-cap behavior.

## Testing

Add regression tests for long failure streaks and repeated HTTP 409 handshakes, with and without a subscribe cursor. Verify capped retry intervals, recovery after a successful handshake, backoff reset on success, and preservation of enrollment and cursor state.

Retry Windows sandbox runner logon once on error 1056 (#49325)

## Why

`CreateProcessWithLogonW` failures with `ERROR_SERVICE_ALREADY_RUNNING` (1056) previously aborted sandbox startup without retrying. At this stage, neither the runner nor the user command has started, so retrying does not replay the command.

## What changed

Retry runner creation once with the same sandbox credentials when logon returns error 1056. Propagate a second failure without refreshing credentials, and keep child startup errors with the same code ineligible for this retry.

## Testing

Add regression tests for recovery, the two-attempt limit, and exclusion of child startup failures. Add a unified exec test that injects a logon failure, verifies that the retry preserves the original request and credentials, and checks that the command runs exactly once.

Notify parent agents when Guardian stops a subagent (#49312)

## Why

A subagent stopped by repeated Guardian denials remained interrupted without notifying its parent. The parent needs guidance to report the stop and wait for explicit user confirmation before continuing the blocked work.

## What changed

Forward `TooManyDenials` interruptions from `MultiAgentV2` children to their parents with Guardian-specific guidance to inform the user and avoid resuming or retrying until the user explicitly confirms. Preserve the child's `Interrupted` status and keep ordinary interruptions silent.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for parent notifications under `CircuitBreakAction::Strict`, silence under `CircuitBreakAction::Default`, and preservation of the child's interrupted status. Add a unit test ensuring long denial messages stay within the notification token limit while retaining the guidance.

Batch metadata reads when resolving thread names (#49305)

## Why

Thread name resolution performs a separate SQLite metadata lookup for each thread. Batch these reads to reduce database queries for large result sets.

## What changed

Add `StateRuntime::get_threads` and use it in `resolve_thread_names`. Fetch metadata in batches of at most 999 IDs to stay within SQLite's bind limit, skipping missing or invalid records independently so valid metadata remains available.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for reads spanning multiple batches, invalid and missing records, duplicate IDs, and empty input.

Compact the inline hidden tag buffer once per chunk (#49300)

## Why

Parsing multiple tag delimiters in a chunk repeatedly drained the pending
buffer, shifting its remaining contents after each delimiter.

## What changed

Track a consumed offset in `InlineHiddenTagParser::push_str` and drain the
buffer once after processing the chunk, preserving partial delimiters for
the next chunk.

## Testing

Add a regression test comparing visible text and extracted tags against
single-chunk parsing at every UTF-8 character boundary. The input covers
non-ASCII text and delimiters, adjacent tags, an empty tag, and an unfinished
tag at end of input.

Scan the session index backwards for batch thread name lookups (#49297)

## Why

Batch thread name lookups read the entire append-only session index even when all requested names could be found near the end.

## What changed

Use `ReverseJsonlScanner` in `spawn_blocking` for `find_thread_names_by_ids`, stopping once every requested ID has a usable name. Preserve the latest nonempty, trimmed name for each ID while skipping malformed entries.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for renamed threads, whitespace-only names, Unicode, reads across chunk boundaries, malformed entries, a partial final write, and missing IDs.
